opportunities.title: Mitsui & Co. Co-Creation Fund - second-round 2026 solicitation (selection end of March 2027)
opportunities.program: Mitsui & Co. Co-Creation Fund (successor channel to the Mitsui & Co. Environment Fund)
opportunities.deadline_text: The deadline of application is 30th of November 2026.
opportunities.funding_text: About 10-100 million yen per project; two projects selected each year; no award if no project qualifies.
opportunities.duration: Three years from the start of the grant period, with annual continuation reviews
opportunities.eligible_applicants: In principle, the applicant must belong to an organization or group with a juridical personality (NPO, public interest corporation, university, company, government agency, etc.), with approval from the head/authorized signatory; must be able to do an online interview.
opportunities.eligible_countries: No restriction stated: 'No restrictions on type of social issue or region (domestic or overseas)'.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No nationality/country limit stated and any juridical-person organization appears eligible, so CIAT/Bioversity could plausibly lead, BUT a Mitsui & Co. officer or employee must recommend the project and act as 'Co-Creator'. Without an internal Mitsui sponsor the application cannot proceed.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Applicant must be the main executing entity; project must be recommended by a Mitsui officer/employee who agrees to act as Co-Creator.
opportunities.consortium_details: Co-creation with a Mitsui employee required (not a consortium).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Social-issue projects of any type; excluded: for-profit, political or religious activities, projects funding Mitsui's own investments, projects where the applicant is not the main executor.
opportunities.required_documents: Not specified (initial contact via website inquiry form).
opportunities.application_procedure: Contact Mitsui through the website inquiry form before the deadline; Fund Team preliminary review, internal interview/review board, then external reviewers; rounds close end of May and end of November; notifications in September and the following March.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Open thematically (any social issue); a climate-resilient agri-food / digital advisory project could fit, but there is no explicit focus on EO/AI/crop modelling.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Three-year grants of up to JPY 100M could fund staff and multi-year work in Asia/LAC/Africa; Mitsui has a large agri-food and Japan/Asia footprint and the researcher has Japan ties.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team could deliver an applied project; main barrier is securing a Mitsui internal Co-Creator.
opportunities.recommendation: Worth pursuing only if a Mitsui & Co. contact (e.g., agri/food business unit, Mitsui offices in Colombia/Kenya/Viet Nam/Japan) can be found to sponsor. The 30 Nov 2026 round is very tight; the realistic target is the end-May 2027 round.
opportunities.potential_partners: Mitsui & Co. agri-food / nutrition business units; Japanese partners (JIRCAS, Univ. of Tokyo).
opportunities.next_action: Submit an inquiry via the Mitsui sustainability contact form asking whether externally initiated projects can be matched to a Co-Creator and whether personnel costs are eligible; aim for the May 2027 round.

opportunities.title: The Audacious Project (TED) - rolling idea submission for large multi-year initiatives
opportunities.funder: The Audacious Project (TED, with a community of philanthropists)
opportunities.deadline_text: As of June 15, 2025, we are no longer setting a deadline for upcoming cycles. ... Ideas can be shared throughout the year.
opportunities.funding_text: Grant sizes not stated; site reports 70 projects launched in 7 cycles and $8.8b catalyzed (i.e., very large multi-year packages - inference, not stated).
opportunities.duration: Multi-year plans ('shape their ideas into viable multi-year plans'); exact duration Not specified
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Individuals 18+ applying on behalf of a nonprofit, NGO, institution or collaboration; 'Organizations and initiatives should have an annual budget of at least $2M'; must be able to receive philanthropic funds and have core infrastructure.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Alliance/CGIAR meets the $2M budget threshold and is a nonprofit institution, so a submission appears possible; realistically requires a CGIAR-wide or multi-partner, very large-scale idea championed at senior leadership level.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Annual budget of at least $2M; core infrastructure to support the work.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Big, bold, scalable solutions with far-reaching social impact.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit idea via /apply; rolling review; selected ideas are shaped into multi-year plans and launched to philanthropists.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: No thematic call; climate adaptation/food systems at massive scale could fit, but research projects are not the typical profile.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Transformational multi-year funding if a CGIAR-wide flagship (e.g., digital climate advisory for smallholders at scale) were pitched.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires an institutional-level initiative and scale far beyond a single research team.
opportunities.recommendation: Not a researcher-level opportunity; flag to Alliance/CGIAR resource mobilization as a channel for a scaled flagship initiative.
opportunities.potential_partners: CGIAR System, other CGIAR centers, national met services, digital advisory implementers.
opportunities.next_action: Share with the Alliance resource-mobilization team; check the 'Learn if you qualify' criteria before any submission.

monitor_sources.name: About / FAQ
monitor_sources.why: Invitation-only climate spend-down funder (focus Healthy Land and Clean Energy). Official FAQ: 'we do not accept unsolicited proposals.' Typical grants reportedly USD 1-10M (secondary sources). Monitor for policy change or regranting partners.

monitor_sources.name: Apply page
monitor_sources.why: Rolling idea submission (no deadline since June 2025) for orgs with >= USD 2M annual budget; very large multi-year packages (size not stated). Institutional-level channel.

monitor_sources.name: How to partner with us
monitor_sources.why: Mostly strategic partners selected by the foundation (concept note on invitation); applicants must operate in World Bank LMICs. Annual open calls only for Entrepreneurs for Resilience (social enterprises; USD 360k grant pool + up to USD 1M blended), Shine and Charity of the Year; ad-hoc EOIs (e.g., Urban NbS in LMICs, closed 20 Jan 2026). CHF 8.1M total grants approved in 2025.

monitor_sources.name: Climate risk and adaptation (RISK Award, RAIN Challenge)
monitor_sources.why: Funds local projects mainly via competitions: biennial RISK Award (EUR 100,000; 2027 theme 'Homes at risk: Climate resilience for informal settlements') and RAIN Challenge with Global Resilience Partnership (East Africa nature-positive agriculture, up to USD 50k, 12 months). Small grants; watch the 2027 rounds.

monitor_sources.funder: Global Resilience Partnership (with Munich Re Foundation)
monitor_sources.name: GRP Innovation Challenge news
monitor_sources.why: Annual Innovation Challenge (RAIN East Africa agriculture; TECH4Resilience incl. SE Asia); open to non-/for-profit orgs in ODA-eligible countries; up to USD 50k for 12 months. 2026 round closed 22 May 2026; watch for a 2027 round (opened 1 May in 2026).

monitor_sources.name: Climate change programmes
monitor_sources.why: Partnership model (Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance, Urban Climate Resilience Program, CRMC); no open calls; engagement via contact / co-funding. Sizes not stated.

monitor_sources.name: OCP Foundation website
monitor_sources.why: Site returned 403 to automated fetch. Funds agriculture/soil research mainly via strategic partnerships (UM6P, Embrapa, Arvalis, IAEA 2026 partnership) and occasional Morocco-focused calls; no verified open call. Check manually; partnership route via UM6P likely.

monitor_sources.name: Grant programs
monitor_sources.why: Open annual calls. International Grant Program (East/SE/South Asia practitioner exchange; max JPY 5M for 1 yr, JPY 10M for 2 yrs) ran 1 Apr-30 May 2026 (closed). Research Grant Program 2026 closed June 2026. Watch 2027 calls (~April); low thematic fit.

monitor_sources.name: Co-Creation Fund
monitor_sources.why: Two rounds/year (end May, end Nov); JPY 10-100M per project, 3 years, any region; requires a Mitsui employee Co-Creator. Replaces the older Mitsui & Co. Environment Fund.

monitor_sources.name: Grant for Environmental Research Projects
monitor_sources.why: Annual open call (15 Apr-30 Jun); General max JPY 5M (1-2 yrs), Special Subject max JPY 10M (2-3 yrs; FY2027 subject 'Interdisciplinary and/or international research to explore Planetary Health', notice dated 7 Oct 2026). Applicant must belong to a research institution in Japan or be a Japanese national/PR; applicant remuneration excluded. Alliance only as collaborator with a Japan-based PI.

monitor_sources.name: Funding opportunities
monitor_sources.why: Lists own Innovation Challenges (all currently 'Awarded'; e.g., USD 10M Inclusive Growth and Recovery Challenge) and third-party calls (e.g., Rockefeller 'Cities Deliver' USD 50M CfP). Watch for a climate/health data challenge; also https://data.org/our-work/challenges/.

monitor_sources.name: Environment program
monitor_sources.why: Official site blocked automated fetch (403). Secondary sources: no unsolicited proposals; funds via invitation and occasional competitions. Very large grants. Monitor for climate RFPs/competitions.

monitor_sources.name: FAQs
monitor_sources.why: Invitation-only: 'We do not currently accept unsolicited applications, but we are exploring alternative models.' Climate risk is one of three funding areas. Grant size not stated. Watch for new open models.

monitor_sources.name: Procurement
monitor_sources.why: Not a grantmaker; issues RFPs/consultancy tenders (e.g., Sierra Leone climate vulnerability maps/data platform, posted 21 Jul 2026; Morocco climate-resilient seeds risk assessment, posted 26 Jan 2026). Service contracts; deadlines in each notice.

monitor_sources.name: Grant-making
monitor_sources.why: Africa-led climate funder (Cape Town) using strategic grantmaking, fiscal hosting and incubation; grantees identified by the foundation (no unsolicited proposals). New 2026-2030 strategy published May 2026. Size not stated officially.
